newsitem.title: MONACO: SOCCER SHOWCASE-PEN PICTURES OF MONACO PLAYERS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-PEN PICTURES OF MONACO PLAYERS.

text.p: Pen pictures of Monaco players most likely to play in Sunday's French first division match against Paris St Germain:

Fabien Barthez, goalkeeper, age 25. Former Marseille keeper pushing PSG's Bernard Lama for France's number one shirt. Won his fourth cap against Portugal on Wednesday night. Superb reflexes and decisive coming out of goal.
Patrick Blondeau, right back, 28. Has just won his first call up to the France squad late in his career. Turns 29 next Monday. Good marker who likes to join attack at every opportunity.
Franck Dumas, central defender, 29. Team captain, strong, hard-tackling centre-back with keen positional sense, very diffcult to get past.
Martin Djetou, central defender, 22. Young player who joined from Strasbourg in the off-season to replace France international Lilain Thuram who left for Italy's Parma. One cap.
Lilian Martin, left back, 25. Done well as an understudy to long term injury victim Eric Di Meco, has a good shot from free kicks.

Emmanuel Petit, libero or defensive midfielder, 26. Has played more than 200 league games for his only club since rising up through the ranks. Fine positional sense and good distributor of the ball. A strong physical presence. Coming back from a knee injury. Has 15 French caps.
Philippe Leonard, utility defender or midfielder, 22. Belgian international who joined from Standard Liege in the off-season and has alternated between spells in the team and on the bench.
Sylvain Legwinski, defensive midfielder, 23. Product of club's junior sides, busy player who compensates for apparent physical fragility with good positional sense and never-say-die spirit.
John Collins, ballwinner and playmaker, 28. Scottish international who joined from Glasgow Celtic in off-season and quickly established himself as first choice on the left of midfield.
Enzo Scifo, attacking midfielder, 30. Belgium's captain who has missed most of the season with a toe injury but is now fully recovered. At the hub of Monaco attacks.
Ali Benarbia, playmaker, 28. Usually at his best in tandem with Scifo, has had a fine season dictating play in the absence of the Belgian. Has excellent vision.
Marco Grassi, forward, 28. Swiss international who has finally overcome exzema of the foot that kept him out for most of the season. Good in the air.

Thierry Henry, striker, 19. Brilliant teenager nurtured by the club, now caught in the middle of a tug-of-war with Spain's Real Madrid. Given his league debut in 1994 when he had barely turned 17 by current Arsenal manager Arsene Wenger.
Anderson, striker, 26. Brazilian emblem of Monaco's title hopes who has already contributed a club top score of 11 league goals, averaging one every two matches. Opportunist with fine ball skills.
Victor Ikpeba, striker, 23. Member of Nigeria's Olympic gold medal team and Anderson's usual strike partner who has been prolific in Monaco's progress to the UEFA Cup quarter-finals.
